thesis: NVIDIA earns a growth purchase from 124% operating-income growth, 66.24% operating margin and $21.341bn quarterly FCF after substantial working-capital absorption. The bull answers accounting-only and funding-fragility objections with positive H1 cash and a $23.220bn liquid surplus excluding equity marks. Concentrated collections and the extended chart constrain conviction, while the 15.14x forward estimate is a scenario rather than guaranteed cheapness.
strongest_counterexample: Receivables absorbed $22.346bn and inventory $5.784bn in Q2; concentrated customer spending or impaired collection could reduce both realized cash and the earnings underpinning the forecast multiple.
invalidation_conditions: A comparable quarter with FCF at or below zero while receivable cash absorption exceeds $22.346bn would invalidate demonstrated conversion resilience.
Year-on-year operating-income decline in two consecutive reported quarters would falsify the sustained profitable-demand thesis.
decisive_factors: Cash remains positive after the specified receivable and inventory burden.
Operating growth excludes equity gains; liquid capacity does not count risky equity investments or erase export/customer concentration.
